Biological interpretation: genes and pathways

Source: vignettes/articles/biological-interpretation.Rmd
biological-interpretation.Rmd

For omics data, the question after clustering is biological: which genes separate the clusters, and which pathways do those genes implicate. MosaiClusteR connects clusters to genes and gene sets through a set of functions that build on Bioconductor.

Dependencies

This layer uses Bioconductor packages (limma, MLP, biomaRt, org.Hs.eg.db), declared under Suggests. Install the ones a function names:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("limma", "MLP", "biomaRt", "org.Hs.eg.db"))

Each function raises a clear error naming the exact install command if a package is missing, so you only install what you use.

Differential features per cluster

DiffGenes() finds the genes that distinguish the clusters, using limma by default. DiffGenesSelection() restricts the test to a chosen set of objects, and FindGenes() looks up genes of interest.

library(MosaiClusteR)
# geneExpr is a genes-by-samples expression matrix aligned to the objects in L
dg <- DiffGenes(List = L, geneExpr = geneExpr, nrclusters = 3, method = "limma")

Pathway enrichment

From the differential genes, test which gene sets are enriched per cluster:

Function Purpose
PathwayAnalysis, Pathways enrichment per cluster
PathwaysIter, PathwaysSelection iterate over clusters, or a chosen selection
PreparePathway assemble inputs for the enrichment step
plot_pathways, PlotPathways visualise enriched terms
enriched_features turn characterisation output into per-cluster term tables 
pa <- PathwayAnalysis(List = L, geneExpr = geneExpr, nrclusters = 3,
                      method = c("limma", "MLP"), geneSetSource = "GOBP")
plot_pathways(pa, style = "circular")     # also "dotplot" and "lollipop"

plot_pathways() offers three layouts. The "dotplot" and "lollipop" styles rank terms in a column; the "circular" style groups terms by cluster around a central hub, with bar length encoding significance and colour encoding the cluster. Pass cluster_cols to match the colours used elsewhere in your figures.

Shared genes and pathways across solutions

When you have several clusterings, ask what they agree on biologically:

Function Purpose
Geneset.intersect, Geneset.intersectSelection gene sets shared across solutions
SharedGenesPathsFeat genes, pathways and features shared across solutions
SharedSelection, SharedSelectionLimma, SharedSelectionMLP shared results for a chosen selection 
shared <- Geneset.intersect(PathwaysOutput = pa)

A short interpretation workflow 

lab <- mosaic_labels(
  SNF(L, type = "data", distmeasure = rep("euclidean", length(L)),
      normalize = rep(FALSE, length(L)), method = rep(list(NULL), length(L))), 3)

dg <- DiffGenes(List = L, geneExpr = geneExpr, nrclusters = 3, method = "limma")
pa <- PathwayAnalysis(List = L, geneExpr = geneExpr, nrclusters = 3,
                      method = c("limma", "MLP"), geneSetSource = "GOBP")
plot_pathways(pa, style = "dotplot")

Cluster first, confirm the clusters are stable and separated, then read their biology from the differential genes and the enriched pathways.
